bambuddy.reason.missing_permissions: The key is valid, but rights Reprintbuddy needs are missing, in its owner's group or at the key itself (see the list). Nothing was saved.
rights.title: Bambuddy right missing
rights.intro: This version of Reprintbuddy needs a right that is still missing. For each missing right the list below shows the group right and the key right that covers it at the key; Reprintbuddy cannot tell which of the two is missing.
rights.still_missing: Checked again: Bambuddy still reports a missing right.
bambuddy.user.key_rights_after: After the key has been created, these three rights may be removed again; the key does not need them.
bambuddy.user.key_rights: Only to create the key in the next step, the group also needs these three rights. Reprintbuddy does not check them. Bambuddy shows the rights in English only, so they are named as there:
permission.library:read_all: so that Reprintbuddy sees your print files
permission.queue:read_all: so that Reprintbuddy sees the whole queue
permission.queue:create: so that Reprintbuddy can queue reprints
permission.queue:start_unreviewed: so that reprints start without approval
permission.printers:read: so that Reprintbuddy sees the printers and their state
permission.inventory:read: so that Reprintbuddy reads the filament stock
permission.filaments:read: to tell whether Bambuddy keeps the spools itself or in Spoolman
bambuddy.where.group: Group right: if the group "Reprintbuddy" lacks it, add it there
bambuddy.where.key: Key right {right}: if the key lacks it, create a new key
bambuddy.key.step3: Set the key exactly like this:
keyright.name: Name
keyright.status: so that Reprintbuddy can read the state of Bambuddy
keyright.queue: so that Reprintbuddy can queue its jobs
keyright.library: only for uploading print files; works only as far as the group allows
bambuddy.user.title: Create a group and a user in Bambuddy
bambuddy.user.why: Reprintbuddy needs its own group in Bambuddy, because none of the system groups fits: "Operators" only sees its own files and queue entries, and "Administrators" may do everything.
bambuddy.user.group: In Bambuddy open Settings → Users and create a group named "Reprintbuddy" with exactly these rights (the internal name is in brackets):
bambuddy.user.user: Then create the user "reprintbuddy" and put it in this group.
bambuddy.user.password: The password of this user is needed only once, to create the key in the next step. Reprintbuddy neither asks for it nor stores it.
bambuddy.user.later: You can add a missing right to the group at any time; no new key is needed for that.
bambuddy.key.title: Create the API key
bambuddy.key.intro: A key always belongs to the user who is signed in when it is created. So do this as the new user:
bambuddy.key.step1: Sign out of Bambuddy and sign in as "reprintbuddy".
bambuddy.key.step2: Open Settings → API keys → Create key.
bambuddy.key.step4: Copy the key at once. Bambuddy shows it only one time.
bambuddy.key.later: The rights of a key cannot be changed afterwards in Bambuddy: its pages only create and delete keys. If a right at the key is wrong, create a new key like this and enter it under Settings → Bambuddy.
bambuddy.connect.title: Enter the address and the key
bambuddy.connect.intro: Reprintbuddy asks Bambuddy whom the key belongs to and what it may really do. The key is saved only if it has every right Reprintbuddy needs.
bambuddy.result.fix: A missing right of the group "Reprintbuddy" is added there; you do not need a new key. If a right is missing at the key itself (e.g. "Read Status"), you need a new key, because Bambuddy's interface does not let you change the rights of an existing key.
bambuddy.admin_warning: Saved. The key belongs to an administrator and may do more than Reprintbuddy needs. It is safer to use the user "reprintbuddy" from the guide.

ops.export.text: Download all data as a JSON file. API keys, passwords, the private HTTPS key and the session secret are never included.

ops.backup.title: Full backup
ops.backup.text: Download the whole database as one file: all data and settings, including the Bambuddy key, the password hash, the private HTTPS key and the session secret. With a password the file is encrypted; without that password it cannot be restored. Restore it under “Restore”, also on a new installation.
ops.backup.warning: Without a password, anyone who has the file gets the keys and can sign in. Keep an unencrypted backup as safe as the server itself.
ops.restore.title: Restore
ops.restore.text: Replace all data with a full backup. First the current database is backed up as before an update. Then Reprintbuddy restarts, and everybody signs in with the account of the backup.
ops.restore.file_hint: A .zip file from “Download backup”, at most 128 MB. It is checked before anything is replaced.
ops.restore.older: The database is from an older version; Reprintbuddy migrates it at the start.
ops.restore.warning: All current data is replaced by the backup. Everybody is signed out.
ops.restore.password_needed: This backup is encrypted. Enter its password.
ops.restore.wrong_password: The password is wrong. Nothing was changed.
ops.restore.retry: The check could not be finished, and the file is not the cause (for example the disk is full). Nothing was changed. The uploaded file is still here: fix the problem and try again.
ops.restore.confirm_subtitle: What the uploaded backup contains, before it replaces the current data.
ops.restore.done_subtitle: The data of the backup is in place; Reprintbuddy restarts with it.
ops.restore.done: Sign in with the user name and password of the backup.
ops.restore.restart_failed: The backup is restored, but Reprintbuddy could not restart. Restart Reprintbuddy now: sign in with the account of the backup, then Settings → General → “Restart Reprintbuddy”. Changes are paused until then.
ops.restore.in_progress: A restore is running. Changes are paused until Reprintbuddy has restarted.
ops.restore.restart_pending: The backup is restored. Restart Reprintbuddy now (Settings → General); changes are paused until then.
ops.msg.backup_mismatch: The two passwords do not match. Nothing was downloaded.
ops.msg.backup_length: The password needs 8 to 1024 characters. Nothing was downloaded.
ops.msg.backup_failed: The backup could not be made. Nothing was downloaded.
ops.msg.restore_foreign: This is not a Reprintbuddy backup. Nothing was changed.
ops.msg.restore_too_new: This backup comes from a newer version of Reprintbuddy. Update first, then restore. Nothing was changed.
ops.msg.restore_too_large: The file is too large (at most 128 MB). Nothing was changed.
ops.msg.restore_damaged: The backup is damaged. Nothing was changed.
ops.msg.restore_incompatible: This backup does not hold a database this version of Reprintbuddy can use. Nothing was changed.
ops.msg.restore_failed: The restore failed. Nothing was changed.
ops.msg.restore_expired: No checked backup file is waiting. Choose the file again.
ops.msg.restore_busy: An update or another restore is running. Nothing was changed.

assembly.subtitle: Booking assembled units: bought parts are used up and the stock grows
info.units_per_print: How many units one print of this plate yields, usually 1. Reprintbuddy uses it to work out how many prints a reprint needs.
info.target: Where Bambuddy sends the print: to a printer model, so any free printer of that model prints it, or to one particular printer.
info.min_stock: A reprint is due when the available units (stock minus reserved) plus everything already planned, printing, awaiting inspection or awaiting assembly fall below this number. Minimum stock 0 and buffer 0: never by itself.
info.buffer: A reprint fills up not just to the minimum stock but to minimum stock plus buffer.
info.needs_assembly: Good units from inspection first wait for assembly and only count as stock after “Book assembled”; the bought parts are deducted then.
info.auto_enabled: On: Reprintbuddy plans reprints of this article by itself as soon as it drops below the minimum stock, and passes them to Bambuddy bit by bit until minimum stock plus buffer is reached. Only works while the main automation switch is on too; off: Reprintbuddy only shows that a reprint is due.
info.has_parts: Enter which bought parts go into this article and how many per unit. They are taken off the parts stock when a unit becomes stock: at inspection “good”, with manual work only at assembly, and when booking in with “Deduct parts”.
info.part_min_stock: Below this stock the part shows as “below minimum” and Reprintbuddy suggests an order, even if no article needs it.
info.pack_size: How many pieces come in one pack. Order suggestions always count whole packs.
info.min_order_packs: The fewest packs one order may have.
info.lead_time_days: Days from ordering to arrival. Order suggestions include what is used during this time.
info.safety_value: Reserve that should still be left after the lead time: as a quantity or as so many days of usage (unit next to it). If it would get tighter, Reprintbuddy suggests an order.
info.consume_parts: Takes the bought parts this article needs off the parts stock for every unit booked in. Untick it when the parts were already deducted.
info.host: Network address Reprintbuddy listens on. 0.0.0.0 means: on all networks of the machine. Takes effect after a restart.
info.inspection_scrap: How many of the finished pieces of a print are scrap (default 0). The rest count as good. Scrap is written off and a replacement print goes to the front of the queue.
info.filament_lead_time: Days from ordering to arrival. A suggestion appears when the stock minus the planned demand minus the use during this time falls below the safety stock.
info.filament_pack_grams: Grams on one spool, the unit in which this sort is bought. Suggestions always count whole spools and round up.
info.filament_safety: Reserve that should still be left after the lead time: as grams or as so many days of usage (unit next to it). If it would get tighter, Reprintbuddy suggests an order.
info.filament_min_order_packs: The fewest spools one order may have. A suggestion is never smaller.
info.filament_mapping: Stock and demand count only ticked spool sorts; a slot without a tick does not count. Reorder suggestions are made for the reordered spool sort, and its stock is the sum of all sorts ticked in its slots. Which spool Bambuddy takes when printing is up to Bambuddy.
info.reorder_packs: How many order units you are ordering, filled in with the suggestion. After “mark as ordered” this amount counts as on its way, and the suggestion does not come back until it has arrived.
articles.not_sliced: Not sliced – slice it first and put the sliced file (.gcode.3mf) into Bambuddy.
articles.relink_subtitle: Choose another print file for this article
settings.invalid_label_host: Enter the printer as an IP address or a name, without http://, without a port, and not this computer.
settings.qr_keep_address: A printed QR code keeps the address it had when it was printed. If the address of the server changes, or the address entered here, print the labels again.
labels.title: Label
labels.printer_address_hint: The IP address or name of the Brother label printer in your network (QL-810W or QL-820NWB). Empty: no printer, nothing is printed.
labels.printer_placeholder: e.g. 192.0.2.50 or the name of the printer
labels.roll_hint: The roll that is in the printer. Before every print Reprintbuddy asks the printer which roll it holds.
labels.raster_hint: Set the printer's command mode to "Raster" once, at the printer (a new printer is set to "P-touch Template" and then prints nothing).
labels.landscape_hint: Labels are always printed in landscape.
labels.content_hint: The QR code of the article is always on the label. Tick what else should be printed next to it; the letters are as large as everything fits. With too many details the last ones are left off; the preview names them.
labels.field.name: Name
labels.preview_alt: The label as it will be printed
labels.preview_hint: This is the picture that is sent to the printer.
labels.cut_warning: A line is too long for the label and is cut off with … . Untick a detail or shorten the text.
labels.note_missing: The label font does not have at least one character and prints it as an empty box. Replace the character in the name or the label text.
labels.note_rtl: The text has letters that are read from right to left. The label prints them from left to right, so they come out the wrong way round.
labels.note_rows: Not all details fit on the label; the last ones were left off. Untick another detail. Missing:
labels.preview_failed: The preview could not be updated. The picture and the notes may be out of date.
labels.note_fine: The address for QR codes is so long that the dots of the code become very fine, and phones read it less well. Enter a shorter address.
labels.hint: Before printing, Reprintbuddy asks the printer which roll is in and whether the cover is closed. If the printer does not answer, it prints anyway.
labels.keep_address: A printed QR code keeps the address it had when it was printed. If the address of the server changes, print the labels again.
labels.not_configured: No label printer is set up.
labels.to_settings: Enter its address under Settings, Labels
labels.copies_invalid: Enter a number of labels from 1 to {max}.
labels.partial: {printed} of {requested} labels sent, then it stopped: {reason} The labels already sent may still be printing; check the printer before you print again.
labels.err.address: The address of the printer in the settings cannot be used.
labels.err.unreachable: The printer cannot be reached at that address.
labels.err.aborted: The connection to the printer broke while sending.
labels.err.busy: Another label is being printed right now; try again in a moment.
labels.err.deadline: The time for this many labels ran out.
labels.err.generic: The label could not be printed.
labels.problem.cover_open: The cover of the printer is open. Nothing was sent; close it and print again.
labels.problem.roll_empty: The roll in the printer is used up. Nothing was sent.
labels.problem.no_roll: There is no roll in the printer. Nothing was sent.
labels.problem.cutter: The cutter of the printer is jammed. Nothing was sent.
labels.problem.error: The printer reports an error. Nothing was sent; check the printer.
labels.problem.wrong_roll: The printer holds another roll ({inserted}) than the one in the settings ({expected}). Nothing was sent. Insert the right roll or change the roll in the settings.
upload.title: Upload print file
upload.subtitle: Target in Bambuddy's file manager: {path}
upload.file_hint: A sliced 3MF file (.gcode.3mf), at most {mb} MB. Afterwards you choose the plate and create the article.
upload.file_hint_relink: A sliced 3MF file (.gcode.3mf), at most {mb} MB. Afterwards you choose the plate for this article.
upload.external: This folder is linked into Bambuddy from outside (external folder). Reprintbuddy only works with files stored in Bambuddy's own file manager, so nothing can be uploaded here. Choose another folder.
upload.folder_gone: This folder no longer exists in Bambuddy.
upload.no_right: The stored key may not upload files. Uploading needs two rights in Bambuddy, and Bambuddy does not say which of them is missing:
upload.no_right_group_where: in the group “Reprintbuddy” – add it there, the key stays
upload.no_right_key_where: at the API key – Bambuddy cannot change a key's rights: sign in as the user reprintbuddy, create a new key with “Read Status”, “Manage Queue” and “Manage Library”, enter it under Settings → Bambuddy and delete the old key
upload.no_right_rest: Everything else in Reprintbuddy works without these rights.
upload.no_right_key: Bambuddy refused the file: the API key lacks “Manage Library”. Bambuddy cannot change a key's rights: create a new key with “Read Status”, “Manage Queue” and “Manage Library” and enter it under Settings → Bambuddy.
upload.no_right_group: Bambuddy refused the file: the group “Reprintbuddy” lacks “Upload Library” (library:upload). Add it there; the key stays.
upload.folder_not_writable: Bambuddy does not let Reprintbuddy put files into this folder.
upload.unclear: It is not clear whether Bambuddy received the file. Look into Bambuddy's file manager before you upload it again.
upload.found_after_unclear: Bambuddy's answer got lost, but the file arrived.
upload.same_name: A file named {name} is already in this folder. Rename your file and upload it again, or use the existing one.
upload.same_name_unsliced: A file named {name} is already in this folder. It is not sliced, so Reprintbuddy cannot use it. Rename your file and upload it again.
upload.use_existing: Create the article from the existing file
upload.use_existing_relink: Choose the existing file for this article
upload.duplicate: Bambuddy already holds the same content as {name}.
upload.bambuddy_not_sliced: Bambuddy does not take {name} for a sliced file. It is now in Bambuddy's file manager, but Reprintbuddy cannot use it.
upload.error.name_invalid: Bambuddy does not accept this name: it must not contain < > : " / \ | ? * or control characters and must not end with a space or a dot.
upload.error.name_too_long: The name is too long for Bambuddy (at most 255 bytes).
upload.error.not_3mf: Only 3MF files (.3mf or .gcode.3mf) can be uploaded.
upload.error.too_large: The file is larger than 200 MB.
upload.error.not_zip: This is not a readable 3MF file.
upload.error.not_sliced: The file is not sliced: it holds no G-code. Slice it first and upload the sliced file (.gcode.3mf).
bambuddy.user.optional: Recommended, not required – only to upload print files from Reprintbuddy:
permission.library:upload: only to upload print files from Reprintbuddy (optional)
bambuddy.result.optional: Not required, only to upload print files:
bambuddy.upload_right_ok: Print files can be uploaded from Reprintbuddy with this key.
bambuddy.upload_right_missing: Uploading print files from Reprintbuddy is not possible with this key: it needs “Upload Library” in the group and “Manage Library” at the key. Everything else works.
